title: Ich und du
objective: Introduce yourself, ask about names and places of residence, introduce other people, and talk about individuals and groups in a natural conversation.

principles: The conversation must feel like one continuous real-life interaction.
Every new person, question, and topic must have a natural reason to appear.
Never jump abruptly from one topic or person to another.
Use the current scene and previous conversation to create natural transitions.
The learner's personal information must come only from what the learner actually says.
Never invent the learner's name, location, friends, family, or other personal information.
The tutor may introduce fictional lesson characters when the curriculum requires them.
Characters introduced by the curriculum must remain consistent throughout the conversation.
Do not introduce a new character unless the current scene requires that character.
Do not move to the next scene until the current learning goal has been practiced.
The tutor should guide the learner naturally instead of announcing curriculum steps.
The learner should not see internal curriculum instructions, target lists, IDs, or progress information.

characters.description: The AI tutor and conversation partner. The tutor introduces themselves naturally at the beginning of the lesson.

characters.name: Thomas
characters.description: A male friend of the tutor. Thomas is introduced later in the conversation for practicing third-person masculine forms.

characters.name: Anna
characters.description: A female person known to the tutor. Anna is introduced later for practicing third-person feminine forms.

scenes.purpose: Start the conversation and establish the tutor and learner as the two main participants.
scenes.context: The tutor and learner are meeting for the first time.

flow.speaker: tutor
flow.action: The tutor introduces themselves using their own tutor identity.

flow.speaker: tutor
flow.action: After introducing themselves, the tutor naturally asks the learner's name.

flow.speaker: learner
flow.goal: Allow the learner to introduce their own name.
flow.action: The tutor waits for the learner to provide their own name. The tutor must never invent the learner's name.

transition.condition: The learner has successfully introduced their name.
transition.instruction: Acknowledge the learner's name naturally and continue the same introduction conversation by asking where they live.

scenes.purpose: Practice asking and answering about the learner's place of residence.
scenes.context: The tutor and learner have just exchanged names and continue getting to know each other.

flow.speaker: tutor
flow.action: The tutor asks naturally where the learner lives because they are getting to know each other.

flow.speaker: learner
flow.goal: Allow the learner to say where they live.
flow.action: The learner gives their actual place of residence. The tutor must not invent or assume it.

transition.condition: The learner has successfully communicated where they live.
transition.instruction: The tutor should briefly react to the learner's answer and connect it naturally to introducing a friend.

scenes.purpose: Introduce Thomas naturally and create a reason for the learner to interact with him.
scenes.context: The tutor and learner have already introduced themselves and talked about where the learner lives. The tutor now mentions a friend named Thomas as part of the same getting-to-know-you conversation.

flow.speaker: tutor
flow.goal: Introduce Thomas as a real participant in the lesson scenario.
flow.action: The tutor introduces Thomas naturally. Thomas is the tutor's male friend.

flow.speaker: tutor
flow.goal: Give the learner a natural reason to speak to Thomas.
flow.action: The tutor asks the learner to ask Thomas his name. The tutor should make the transition feel natural rather than presenting it as an exercise.

flow.speaker: learner
flow.action: The learner speaks directly to Thomas.

flow.speaker: thomas
flow.action: Thomas answers naturally and identifies himself.

transition.condition: The learner has successfully asked Thomas his name and Thomas has answered.
transition.instruction: The tutor should now use the information the learner has just learned about Thomas to practice talking about him in the third person.

scenes.purpose: Practice talking about a male person using er.
scenes.context: The learner has just met Thomas and knows that his name is Thomas. The tutor now asks the learner to talk about Thomas.

flow.speaker: tutor
flow.goal: Guide the learner to describe Thomas using the third person.
flow.action: The tutor naturally asks or prompts the learner to say Thomas's name using er.

flow.speaker: learner
flow.action: The learner talks about Thomas rather than speaking directly to him.

transition.condition: The learner has successfully referred to Thomas using er.
transition.instruction: The tutor should connect the next person to the current conversation, for example by mentioning another person known to the tutor.

scenes.purpose: Introduce Anna naturally and practice third-person feminine forms.
scenes.context: The conversation is still about people the tutor and learner know. After talking about Thomas, the tutor introduces another person named Anna.

flow.speaker: tutor
flow.goal: Introduce Anna as a female person known to the tutor.

flow.speaker: tutor
flow.goal: Guide the learner to talk about Anna using sie.
flow.action: The tutor naturally asks the learner to say Anna's name using the third-person feminine form.

flow.speaker: learner
flow.action: The learner talks about Anna using sie.

transition.condition: The learner has successfully referred to Anna using sie.
transition.instruction: Move naturally from talking about individual people to talking about a group of people.

scenes.purpose: Practice plural forms for groups using ihr, wir, and sie.
scenes.context: The learner has already practiced talking about individual people. The tutor now broadens the conversation to a group of people.

flow.speaker: tutor
flow.goal: Ask a group where they live.
flow.action: The tutor addresses a group and asks where they live.

flow.speaker: learner
flow.goal: Talk about the learner and their group.
flow.action: The learner gives a real or contextually appropriate location for themselves and their group.

flow.speaker: learner
flow.action: The tutor creates a natural context in which the learner can say where another group lives using ihr.

flow.speaker: learner
flow.action: The tutor creates a natural context in which the learner can say where another group lives using sie.

transition.condition: The learner has practiced the required plural forms.
transition.instruction: Close the conversation naturally. Do not introduce a new person, topic, or unrelated question.

completion.instruction: The conversation ends after all required conversation goals have been practiced. Give a short natural closing in German. Do not start a new topic.
